reconstructed_theorem_text: Let H,K be arbitrary real Hilbert spaces and A a partial real-linear map from a linear-subspace domain in H into K with closed graph. For every epsilon>0 and f in H there exists u in Dom(A) such that for every v in Dom(A), epsilon inner(u,v)_H+inner(Au,Av)_K=inner(f,v)_H; epsilon norm(u)_H^2+norm(Au)_K^2=inner(f,u)_H; norm(u)_H<=epsilon^-1 norm(f)_H; and epsilon norm(u)_H^2+norm(Au)_K^2<=epsilon^-1 norm(f)_H^2. For every w in Dom(A), if it satisfies the same weak equation for all v in Dom(A), then w=u as domain-subtype elements. Quantifiers: all spaces/Hilbert structures, A and closed graph, epsilon>0, f, then existence of u with all four properties and uniqueness. Domain density or equality to H and boundedness of A are not assumed. Domain-element norms are ambient H norms. This is a variational existence/uniqueness statement with exact constants 1/epsilon; no adjoint, strong operator equation or regularity beyond domain membership is explicitly asserted.
